column1: # KT14: the audit of every `unsafe` in kernel/src (2026-11-23). file, hash of the block and its SAFETY comment (scripts/unsafe_inventory.py), verdict (ok | weak | bug), the condition and why it holds or the problem and its item. A changed block has a new hash and is audited again.

AIMED Vec is sized once in discover (boot, one hart) and never resized; afterwards only the AtomicUsize elements change, so a shared reference and bounds-checked get() are sound from any hart

send_ipi: index < hart_order.len() by position(); page imsic_base+index*0x1000 is one of aia::pages(), refused by discover if it overlaps RAM/reserved or exceeds the direct map, and mapped RW by kmem::init; aiatree checks the reg window covers one page per hart and refuses grouped/guest layouts; volatile u32 write of seteipnum_le at offset 0; other harts doing the same is just more MMIO
INFO is written once by discover (only caller kmem::init, kmem.rs:468, boot hart, interrupts off, before smp::start_secondaries) and never again; shared read of an Option afterwards cannot race

[T242] aim_and_unmask: comment explains the register protocol but not the safety condition, which is that the controller exists (reg() silently uses physical base 0 when info() is None) and irq is an admitted source 1..=62 (irq 0 underflows irq-1 into a wild address; irq > 1023 leaves the 4 mapped pages). It holds: info() is Some via the hart_order lookup above; enable() is called only after irq != 0 && irq_allowed (user/trap.rs:1173-1192) and reenable() only with the irq of an Interrupt object, created solely at that site. User mode cannot pick another irq; concurrent harts only race device writes

retarget_from: s iterates info().sources (1..=62) with info() Some, index is a position in hart_order; TARGET+4*(s-1) lies in the mapped fourth APLIC page; volatile u32 write; a racing aim_and_unmask on another hart only changes which hart gets the message

claim: csrrw stopei,x0 reads and clears the top pending id of this hart's own IMSIC file, register-only (out(reg)); only caller external_trap on scause interrupt 9, which can fire only after init_hart set SEIE on a hart with Ssaia; interrupts are off in the trap

init: info() is Some (checked), APLIC's 4 pages validated against RAM and mapped by kmem::init before aia::init (main.rs:153); sources are 1..=62 (aiatree) so SOURCECFG+4*(s-1) <= 0xf8 and no underflow; volatile u32 accesses to documented registers; boot hart, interrupts off (comment mentions 'the target' which this block does not write: stale wording only)

[T242] disable: comment names the register only. The unstated condition is that a controller exists, because reg() falls back to physical base 0 when info() is None and would write direct_base+0x1fdc. It holds on both paths: deliver() calls it after irq_allowed(source) (needs info Some) and wake.rs:142 only for an Interrupt object, which can exist only if irq_allowed passed at creation. CLRIENUM offset is fixed, so the irq value cannot move the address

init_hart: Ssaia siselect/sireg writes for eidelivery/eithreshold/eie0 then sie.SEIE, touching only this hart's file; callers aia::init (boot hart, AIA found in tree) and secondary_main (smp.rs:46), both with interrupts off and before the thread can migrate, so siselect/sireg pairs are not torn; ids shift < 64 because sources <= 62; operands are in(reg), no memory or stack use; a hart without Ssaia takes an illegal-instruction trap (fatal), not UB

discover runs once from kmem::init on the boot hart with interrupts off before any secondary hart is started (main.rs: kmem::init precedes start_secondaries and irq::enable); earlier info()/aimed() readers are on the same hart and see None/empty; replaces an empty Vec
KASLR_SLIDE is stored once by _start on the boot hart before paging (boot.rs:260) and no Rust or other asm writes it; all readers run after that
KASLR_DIRECT is stored once by _start (boot.rs:262), read-only afterwards; no other writer in the tree
KERNEL_DELTA is stored once by _start (boot.rs:258); the only other use is a read in the secondary entry asm (sbi.rs:124)
csrr sstatus into an output register; no state change

clears then sets CBIE=01, CBCFE and CBZE in this hart's senvcfg and reads it back; only changes which cbo instructions user mode may run on its own mappings; called per hart at boot (main.rs:151, smp.rs:45)
one csrw satp; table liveness and ASID rules are the caller's contract, verified at the three call sites; no flush is the documented L18 design
csrc sstatus of the FS and VS fields only; Off is the kernel's required state (C7, FP3)
fence.i only synchronises this hart's fetches with its stores; no register or memory effect

sets VS to Initial, reads vlenb, clears VS back to Off (the kernel's state, FP3); reads no vector register; callers are boot (main.rs:150) and a secondary's start (smp.rs:44) with interrupts off and after lazy_units_off, so no user state is in the unit
mv from tp into an output register; options are true
sfence.vma zero,zero drops this hart's cached translations (all ASIDs); can only cause re-walks

unsafe fn; contract (token names a live table mapping everything the kernel runs from and touches) holds at all three callers: kmem.rs:569 (table just built by init), kmem.rs:634 and smp.rs:41 (the kernel's own table, KERNEL_ASPACE set before secondaries start)

csrrw rd,seed,x0 is the mandated read form; the one caller (entropy.rs read_zkr) runs only after hart_has_zkr on the boot hart; if M-mode withholds SSEED the read is an illegal instruction and the boot stops in fatal(): fail-stop, no memory effect
csrr satp into a compiler-chosen register: no memory, no state change, legal in S-mode
sfence.vma va,asid with both operands in real registers (never x0) drops one page of one ASID on this hart; flushing too little is a caller concern, not a memory effect of the block
writes tp, which is reserved (never allocated by the compiler, no thread-locals in the kernel); value is the caller's contract, verified in bind

[T242] sound at its one caller (user/mod.rs:136: first init of UserState under irq::without and the object lock, before any process, kernel table installed), but the block needs interrupts off (a switch between the read and the restore would write back a stale satp) and that is only in the doc of a SAFE fn, not in the SAFETY comment or the signature; also the result is taken as every hart's ASID width (only the probing hart is measured)

unsafe fn; contract holds at its callers: kmem.rs:647 (kernel table, ASID 0, always live), user/trap.rs:120 (token from install_token_of under the lock: the running thread's live process, generation flush done) and user/trap.rs:158 (the thread's own binding, generation checked current, hart flushed if it had not seen it)
unsafe fn; both callers are a hart's own boot before any user thread ran on it: thread::init (thread.rs:246) and secondary_main (smp.rs:36)
mv from sp into an output register; nomem/nostack/preserves_flags are all true
wfi only stalls the hart until an interrupt is pending; resumes even with interrupts masked
csrw satp then sfence.vma zero,zero; the table is the caller's guarantee and the kernel half is identical in every table so the next instruction still fetches; per-hart effect only
unsafe fn; sole caller percpu::bind passes &HARTS[index], a 'static per-hart record, first thing on each hart before a trap can be taken (SMP1)
wfi only idles the hart; reached after save_and_disable in the never-returning tail of exit; no memory, stack or register effect

[T242] exit: base is the reg of the first sifive,test0/test1 node, bounded only by DIRECT_MAP_PHYS_LIMIT (finisher::init); it is not checked against RAM, reserved ranges or the image (aia::discover does this for its pages), and kmem.rs:530 maps the page RW unchecked, so a wrong tree turns this into a u32 write into kernel-visible memory. On a sane tree: page mapped by the early table and by kmem::init in non-release builds, and the write is skipped when RELEASE (page unmapped then); volatile u32 is the device's width. Not influenceable from user mode
as line 373, at the end of the locked save path: clears only FS and VS of this hart's sstatus

[T242] true: vs_claim == current tid implies (set only under the lock together with holder and vs_buf) that buf is the Box<VecRegs> of the thread running on this hart; another hart clears this claim only when it loads or saves the same thread, which cannot run in two places, and thread ids are never reused. But the comment says the box lives until thread_gone: it is also dropped and replaced by write_vec's replace_regs; that is safe only because thread_write_state requires the target parked (ksys thread_state_target) and drop_claim clears the claim first. thread_gone runs on the exiting thread itself inside the kernel, not 'for a thread that is not running'

[T242] r.v.len() is checked to be 32*vlenb just above, each vs8r.v writes 8*vlenb at a pointer stepped by that stride, csrs is 4 u64, vstart is saved, zeroed and restored, VS back to Off, vector registers only read; whole-register stores do not depend on vtype/vill. vlenb is the same on every hart (check_hart). Unstated: interrupts off across the block (true: trap context or object lock)

[T242] as the vector case: fs_claim == current tid implies fs_buf is this running thread's Box<FpRegs>; the unstated second freeing path is write_fp's replace_regs, safe because the target must be parked and its claim is dropped first under the lock

[T242] f is r.f (32 u64) and c is r.fcsr (u32) of a live &mut FpRegs, only t is written, FP registers are only read, the unit goes back to Off: true. Unstated and needed: interrupts off for the whole block and this hart's registers holding the thread's state (a preemption between csrs and csrc would save another thread's registers); true on every path (trap context, or the object lock, which asserts interrupts off)

[T242] the four vl8re8.v read 32*vlenb bytes from r.v, but unlike save_into there is NO length check here and the comment does not state one: it holds only because every VecRegs comes from VecRegs::zero(vlenb()) or from write_vec, whose single caller (thread_state_call) checked len == 32 + 32*vlenb; a future caller with a short vector is an out-of-bounds read. User-written vl/vtype/vcsr/vstart go through vsetvl and WARL CSR writes, which cannot trap in S-mode (bad vtype just sets vill). Undeclared v0-v31 clobbers are harmless (kernel is built without V). Interrupts off is needed and unstated

STATE is reached only through state(), and every caller holds the object lock with interrupts off: trap paths lock before trap_entry, user faults reach first_use under the lock, return_to_user locks itself, thread_gone/read_*/write_*/mark_present run inside with_state, entry_count locks (the check itself is a debug_assert, so release builds do not test it)

[T239] the lock makes other harts wait but does not make the &'static mut unique on this hart: write_fp (fp.rs:696-714) and write_vec (740-764) take s = state(), then call drop_claim, which calls state() again and writes harts[h] through a second &mut FpState, then go on using s: two live aliasing &mut (undefined behaviour by Rust's aliasing rules; reachable from user mode by thread_write_state FP/VECTOR on a parked thread). No machine-level corruption seen, but the SAFETY comment only speaks of the lock and context switches, not uniqueness. Fix: pass s into drop_claim. (Same shape one level up: state_write holds with_state's &mut UserState while write_fp -> charge_state -> user::job_of_thread opens with_state again)

[T242] reads 32 u64 from a live &FpRegs, writes f0-f31 and fcsr, unit back to Off. The undeclared FP clobbers are argued in the comment and hold: the kernel runs with FS Off, so compiled code cannot have put a value in an FP register without trapping (it is still outside the letter of the asm! contract on a target with F/D codegen on). Unstated: interrupts must be off across the block; true at both callers of return_to_user (trap exit; lifecycle.rs:146)
csrr sstatus is a side-effect-free read into an out(reg)
csrs sie with STIE only; a timer interrupt is delivered only once SIE is set; callers main.rs:196 and smp.rs:43 run after trap::init and timer::start (stimecmp = MAX)
csrrci sstatus,2 atomically clears SIE and returns the old value into an out(reg); no memory or stack effect; valid in S-mode on any path

enable: sets SIE, so the condition is that a trap can be taken (tp = PerHart, stvec = trap_entry, sscratch = 0, valid kernel stack). Direct callers: main.rs:197 and smp.rs:53 (after percpu::bind, trap::init, timer::start), thread.rs:363 (join_scheduler), thread.rs:528 (thread_bootstrap on a fresh kernel stack), user/lifecycle.rs:82 (after bkl::unlock); restore() re-enables only where interrupts were already on, so it is inductive

[T242] sbi5: register convention is right (a7/a6 ids, a0..a4 in, a0/a1 inlateout; SBI preserves every other register, so no clobber_abi is needed; legacy putchar also returns in a0 only). But the comment says a0-a2 (a0-a4 are passed) and 'changes no kernel state', which is not true of what the safe fn can be asked for: HSM hart_start runs kernel code at a caller-supplied address, hart_suspend, SRST, RFENCE. Soundness rests on the callers, all of which I traced and pass fixed ids and kernel-derived arguments (smp.rs:114/143 with entry_phys = secondary_entry, smp.rs:314/340, DBCN/putchar, SRST, probe via debug_stat 126); user mode controls none of them

unsafe fn; sole caller reschedule (thread.rs:785): interrupts off, lock released by release_all just before, old/new are boxed contexts of the outgoing and the picked thread kept alive until reap_prev after the switch, and transit (TR1/RQ1) keeps any other hart from running old before it is saved; new was saved by a switch or built by Context::new on a live kstack

calls the global_asm context_switch, which stores ra, sp, s0-s11 to old and loads them from new (14 words, the size of Context) and returns on the new stack; tp is deliberately not switched (per hart, SMP1) and no FP state exists in the kernel (C7)
csrr time reads the counter into an out(reg); no side effect (the profile requires Zicntr/Sstc and firmware opens mcounteren.TM; otherwise an illegal-instruction trap, not UB)

csrw stimecmp only (re)schedules this hart's own supervisor timer interrupt; register operand; callers timer::start and timer::program on the running hart; without Sstc/STCE it traps illegal (fatal), not UB
csrr stimecmp is a side-effect-free read into an out(reg); only caller timer::start (boot probe)

instruction_length: only caller is trap_body's Err arm with cause 13/15 (cause != 12 guard) after the SPP=0 early return, so sepc is the kernel instruction that was just fetched and executed: in kernel text, mapped RX (map_image), 2-byte aligned (IALIGN 16), so an aligned u16 read is valid. User mode cannot reach it (user traps return earlier); another hart can only flip EXPECT, which changes whether the arm is taken, not the validity of sepc
csrs scounteren bit 2 (instret) in test builds only (cfg not release or release-suite); selects a user-readable counter, no memory touched

init: stvec = trap_entry (.balign 4, low bits 00 = direct mode, kernel text at its upper-half address, mapped by both the early and the kernel table) and sscratch = 0 (the trap entry's 'from the kernel' marker). Callers main.rs:133 and smp.rs:33, both after percpu::bind put this hart's PerHart in tp (trap_entry reads 0/8/16(tp)) and with interrupts off
csrs scounteren bit 1 only lets user mode read the time counter; no memory touched; per-hart, set in init on every hart
sfence.vma zero,zero flushes this hart's translations; only makes the TLB less stale; legal in S-mode (callers selftest.rs:460 and kmem::flush_tlb)

[T242] Comment says 'clears sstatus.FS only' but the mask (3<<13)|(3<<9) clears FS and VS. Both are intended (kernel runs with FP and vector units off, INVARIANTS FP3; the frame already holds the user's sstatus for the return), register-only, on the from_user path at the top of trap_handler_inner before any FP use; nothing user mode or another hart can change. Comment should say FS and VS
sfence.vma va,zero drops this hart's cached translations of one page for every ASID; no other effect; va comes from the kernel fault's mapped range, and a flush of any address is harmless

Pointer is null or a &'static Location: the only store is lock() writing Location::caller() (static data) into an AtomicPtr; as_ref handles null; a racy Relaxed read can only see null or a previously stored static, so no path makes it dangle.

[T240] write_str: claims exclusivity of static mut LINE from 'interrupts are off', which is not sufficient on SMP; the real guard is the UART lock (with_uart), and break_lock() (panic handler main.rs:309, trap fatal trap.rs:777) zeroes UART_OWNER without stopping other harts, so a panicking hart forms a second &mut LINE while the lock holder on another hart is still inside kernel_text: a data race on LineState (two plain fields, panic path only, low severity). Fix: say 'UART lock held' and make LINE atomics/Cell-free or accept the race explicitly

[T242] try_read: comment says only 'mapped like the transmit ones'. UART_BASE is the ns16550(a) reg of /chosen/stdout-path (fdt::console_base refuses reg-shift != 0 and reg-io-width != 1, so byte-wide volatile access is right) and is only bounded by DIRECT_MAP_PHYS_LIMIT; unlike aia::discover it is never checked against RAM, reserved ranges or the kernel image, and kmem::init (kmem.rs:530) maps that page RW in the direct map unchecked, so a wrong tree makes this write/read kernel memory (breaks M5); also base+5 can cross the mapped page if reg is not page-aligned. True on a sane tree, not reachable from user mode or another hart. Reads LSR/RBR without the UART lock (callers: interactive.rs only), harmless for memory safety

[T242] put: UART_BASE is the ns16550(a) reg of /chosen/stdout-path (fdt::console_base refuses reg-shift != 0 and reg-io-width != 1, so byte-wide volatile access is right) and is only bounded by DIRECT_MAP_PHYS_LIMIT; unlike aia::discover it is never checked against RAM, reserved ranges or the kernel image, and kmem::init (kmem.rs:530) maps that page RW in the direct map unchecked, so a wrong tree makes this write/read kernel memory (breaks M5); also base+5 can cross the mapped page if reg is not page-aligned. True on a sane tree, not reachable from user mode or another hart. Comment's 'nothing else touches them' is also loose (try_read does). Only reached through with_uart closures

[T240] write_user: same as write_str ('as in write_str'): &mut LINE is exclusive only under the UART lock, and a panic or fatal trap on another hart breaks that lock and aliases LINE while this hart is still in user_byte (benign plain-data race, panic path only)

8 header bytes readable through the early table's direct map: locate rejects dtb==0 and dtb+8 above DIRECT_MAP_PHYS_LIMIT, boot.rs maps all 64 GiB RW, u8 reads need no alignment; only caller is kmain with firmware's a1 (firmware trusted to point at RAM, stated); single hart, not user-reachable

[T242] len bounded by locate (40..=256 KiB, end below 64 GiB) and nobody writes the tree (reserved, never in the allocator, never in the RW direct map), so true before kmem::init. After kmem::init the claim 'the tree's frames are direct-mapped read-only' holds only for frames inside the tree's own /memory ranges below the limit: kmem::init silently skips frames failing in_ram(), and the next dtb_blob() reader (require_extensions, boot_arg_*, chaos::init) would fault. Firmware-dependent, not user/hart-reachable; comment states it unconditionally

Reads are of slab-frame headers and pool link words at 8-aligned direct-map addresses of frames taken from kmem::frame_alloc (managed frames, all mapped RW by kmem::init). The unlocked read in small_free (class_of_addr) is of the tag word of a slab holding the live object being freed, which cannot be released meanwhile; only a kernel double/stray free breaks it
unsafe fn required by the trait; the caller's contract (ptr from this allocator with the same layout) is what the inner block relies on

GlobalAlloc contract: small classes are powers of two >= max(size,align) carved at multiples of the class size in page-aligned frames; everything else goes to linked_list_allocator under the irq-off HEAP spinlock; dealloc routes by address and the three ranges are disjoint (direct map slots 256..384, heap window slot 416, boot heap in the image at slot 510)
small_free drain loop: still inside the same interrupts-off section on the owning hart
mag is percpu::this().magazines fetched after irq::save_and_disable in small_alloc, so owner hart with interrupts off (no migration, no re-entry: pop holds no reference across a call)

ptr is non-null and not in the direct map, so it came from the grown heap iff it lies in the heap window, else from the boot heap; HEAP lock held with irqs off; relies on GlobalAlloc::dealloc's caller contract (stated)

Writes come only from Slab/Pool code under the HEAP lock (small_alloc/small_free/return_magazines/rebalance_pool all inside with_heaps) to header and link words of frames the heap owns in the direct map; 8-aligned

HEAP_MEMORY is a private static used nowhere else; heap::init has one caller (kmain, boot hart, before any allocation and before other harts start); linked_list_allocator 0.10.6 aligns the bottom itself
Same hart and same interrupts-off section as the pop in small_alloc (inside with_heaps, whose lock also keeps irqs off); push returns before any other call
small_free: mag fetched after save_and_disable; class comes from the slab header and is bounds-checked inside push
return_magazines: mag fetched after save_and_disable, this hart's record, interrupts off for the whole loop
unsafe fn required by the trait; body has no unsafe of its own beyond small_alloc; null returned when both heaps are exhausted as the contract allows

grow holds KPT for its whole body so `have` is stable and [window+have, +added) was just mapped RW contiguously with frames from the database; HEAP lock held for init/extend. Note (not UB): no remote sfence is sent, and on hardware without Svvptc another hart may hold a cached-invalid entry and take a kernel page fault the handler treats as fatal; QEMU does not do this

BRIDGE_SOCKET is written once by run() before thread::spawn of the bridge and taken once by that thread; run() has one caller (main.rs:242) and the spawn orders the write before the take, so no concurrent access
the only reader (bridge_main) is spawned on the next line, after this write; run() is called once from kmain, so nothing else touches the static

Every caller passes pa inside a managed frame (page-table frames from the database; usercopy::resolve refuses unmanaged pfns so device VMOs never get here; futex words are pa & !7 of a resolved managed frame; copy_frame/zero_frame use pfn<<12 + w*8); managed frames are direct-mapped RW for ever, so even a stale pa cannot fault; 8-aligned at every call site. Concurrent user-mode stores to the same word are tolerated by the volatile read

unsafe fn with a stated contract (the reference must not outlive the guard); its five callers store the guard next to the reference. `expect` only fires if a cell is taken before kmem::init, which boot order prevents

[T242] get(): Each &'static mut comes from a guard stored beside it and dropped after it (field order); Spin::lock is non-recursive (asserts) and irq-off so no second &mut exists. True at every call site (grepped: nobody moves a field out), but the type does not enforce it: the fields are pub and movable, so safe code like `let m = kmem::X().mm;` would compile and dangle after the guard drops; the comment does not say callers must not do this. Also the comment is stale: it says the big kernel lock is 'checked above' and protects 'the address space', but get() checks nothing and Kmem no longer carries an address space
Same single boot-hart call of kmem::init; WINDOWS is first read by user-mode paths much later

[T242] get_as(): Each &'static mut comes from a guard stored beside it and dropped after it (field order); Spin::lock is non-recursive (asserts) and irq-off so no second &mut exists. True at every call site (grepped: nobody moves a field out), but the type does not enforce it: the fields are pub and movable, so safe code like `let m = kmem::X().mm;` would compile and dangle after the guard drops; the comment does not say callers must not do this
kmem::init has one caller (kmain on the boot hart, interrupts off, before start_secondaries); nothing reads USABLE before init returns

The table just built maps text/rodata/data (boot stack, bss, boot heap, per-hart records), the direct map of all usable RAM including the frame metadata and the table's own frames, the tree and the console/finisher/AIA pages; boot hart only
STATS is written once in kmem::init on the boot hart; readers (selftest, debug_stat, user state) run later; Copy read of plain integers

`at` is the page-aligned start of a usable range (RAM minus reserved, image, tree) strictly larger than meta_frames; managed <= usable_total and meta_frames = ceil(usable_total*size_of::<Meta>()/4096) so the slice fits; the early table maps all 64 GiB RW and the kernel table keeps the same address RW; zeroed Meta is valid (repr(C) integers); the managed ranges start after these frames so nothing else gets them
As load: same call sites, object lock and AS lock held from resolve to the compare-exchange, word 4-aligned in a direct-mapped managed frame
KERNEL_HALF is written once by snapshot_kernel_half before the first process is loaded; every caller runs on behalf of a process, so no write can be concurrent with this read

[T242] mem(): Each &'static mut comes from a guard stored beside it and dropped after it (field order); Spin::lock is non-recursive (asserts) and irq-off so no second &mut exists. True at every call site (grepped: nobody moves a field out), but the type does not enforce it: the fields are pub and movable, so safe code like `let m = kmem::X().mm;` would compile and dangle after the guard drops; the comment does not say callers must not do this

All four users (waits.rs futex_lock_pi, futex_unlock_pi, pi_thread_gone x2) resolve the word with va&3==0 to a managed frame and use it inside the same with_state section with the process's AS lock (`_as`) still held; the frame cannot go: unmap needs that AS lock, decommit/set_size run under the object lock, and lock-free teardown_memory only decommits VMOs nobody else holds

[T242] jobs(): Each &'static mut comes from a guard stored beside it and dropped after it (field order); Spin::lock is non-recursive (asserts) and irq-off so no second &mut exists. True at every call site (grepped: nobody moves a field out), but the type does not enforce it: the fields are pub and movable, so safe code like `let m = kmem::X().mm;` would compile and dangle after the guard drops; the comment does not say callers must not do this

[T242] frames(): Each &'static mut comes from a guard stored beside it and dropped after it (field order); Spin::lock is non-recursive (asserts) and irq-off so no second &mut exists. True at every call site (grepped: nobody moves a field out), but the type does not enforce it: the fields are pub and movable, so safe code like `let m = kmem::X().mm;` would compile and dangle after the guard drops; the comment does not say callers must not do this
